who.question: Who is Klyx?

pme.question: Is an AI audit useful for a 15-person company?
pme.answer: Yes, that is often where it pays back fastest. In a company of 10 to 50 people, a few repetitive tasks (quotes, invoices, follow-ups, email triage) take one or two people several hours a week. The audit finds them, puts a number on that time and checks that an automation costs less than what it saves.

duration.question: How long does the audit take?
duration.answer: One to two weeks between the first interview and the review. Interviews take about an hour per person, and we ask your team to show us their tools the way they really use them. The rest happens on our side: mapping, scoring the possible automations and writing the plan. You have nothing to prepare beforehand.

deliverable.question: What do I get at the end?
deliverable.answer: A written document, not a slide deck: the map of your processes, the possible automations scored by hours saved, cost and risk, the GDPR points to settle and a 90-day plan. We go through it together in the review meeting. It belongs to you, and you can hand it to another provider if you prefer.

bpifrance.question: Can your audit be funded by Bpifrance?
bpifrance.answer: Not this one. Bpifrance's Diagnostic Data IA goes through experts it accredits, and Klyx is not one of them. If that funding matters to you, talk to an accredited expert. If you want an answer within two weeks, at a fixed price and with no application to file, our private audit is built for that.

noTech.question: Do I need a tech team to follow the plan?
noTech.answer: No. Most of the small companies we work with have no in-house developer. We write the plan for the person who decides, without jargon, and each recommendation says who can carry it out: you with a tool like Make or n8n, us, or another provider. When a point needs real technical skills, we say so.

whatIs.question: Is GEO just SEO for ChatGPT?
whatIs.answer: Partly. GEO stands for Generative Engine Optimization: the work that makes a site readable and citable by AI engines such as ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini or Google's AI answers. SEO aims for a rank in a list of links. GEO aims for a place among the few sources an AI engine cites in its answer. The two overlap a lot.

guarantee.question: Can you guarantee ChatGPT will cite me?
guarantee.answer: No, and nobody can honestly promise that. AI engines change their answers from one week to the next and do not publish their rules. What we commit to is the method: a baseline, documented fixes on your pages, and the same measurement 30 days later on the same questions. You see what moved, with the numbers to back it.

vsSeo.question: Should I stop doing classic SEO?
vsSeo.answer: No. AI engines rely largely on the same signals as Google: fast, well-structured pages with clear answers and verifiable facts. Good SEO is still the base. GEO adds direct answers at the top of the page, structured data, an llms.txt file and tracking of what AI engines say about you, question by question.

platforms.question: My site runs on WordPress or Webflow. Does that work?

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This page explains what data Klyx collects, why, and how to exercise your rights. The data controller is Maxime Mansiet, sole trader (Klyx), reachable at {email}.

contactForm.title: Contact form
contactForm.body: When you fill in the form, we receive your name, email, company, need, budget and message. This data is used only to reply to you. Messages are sent through Resend, which processes emails on our behalf.

booking.title: Booking a call
booking.body: Call booking runs on Cal.com, which receives what you enter (name, email, time slot). Cal.com's privacy policy applies to that service.

analytics.title: Audience measurement and cookies
analytics.body: We measure traffic on this site with PostHog, on its European infrastructure (PostHog Cloud EU, data hosted in the European Union). It runs without cookies and writes nothing to your browser, neither cookies nor local storage: a visit is not linked to your earlier visits, nor tracked across other sites. We only measure page views, clicks on the booking and quote buttons, and whether a contact form submission succeeded or failed, never its content.
analytics.purpose: Purpose: aggregate traffic statistics, to learn which pages are useful. This data is not combined with any other processing, not shared or sold, not used for advertising, and IP addresses are not kept. This setup meets the conditions the CNIL (French data protection authority) sets for exempting audience measurement from consent, which is why you see no consent banner.
analytics.retention: Retention: 13 months at most, set in Klyx's PostHog project.
analytics.optOut: To object, turn on your browser's "Do Not Track" or "Global Privacy Control" setting: the tool is then not loaded. A content blocker has the same effect. Since nothing is stored on your device, there is no choice for us to record. You can also write to {email}.
analytics.cookies: Apart from that, the site sets a single technical cookie that remembers your display language, and no advertising cookies.

hosting.title: Hosting and transfers
hosting.body: The site is hosted by Netlify, Inc. (United States), which participates in the EU-US Data Privacy Framework. Resend and Cal.com are also US providers. Transfers of data to the United States rely, depending on the provider, on the EU-US Data Privacy Framework or on the European Commission's standard contractual clauses.

prospection.title: Business prospecting by email
prospection.intro: We sometimes email companies to introduce our services. These messages go to professionals, at their work address, and relate to an offer connected to their line of work.
prospection.legalBasis: Legal basis: Klyx's legitimate interest in making its services known (Article 6(1)(f) GDPR). Between businesses, the CNIL (the French data protection authority) allows these emails without prior consent, provided the message relates to the recipient's job and they can easily object to further emails.
prospection.sources: Contact details come from public professional sources, such as the company's website or LinkedIn.
prospection.retention: We keep this data for at most 3 years after your last contact.
prospection.optOut: To stop receiving emails, reply to the email and say so, or write to {email}. Your address then goes on a suppression list and we won't contact you again.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: You can ask to access, correct or delete your data, object to its processing or request its portability by writing to {email}. We reply within one month. If you believe your rights aren't respected, you can complain to the CNIL (cnil.fr).

faq.title: Questions about AI in a real estate agency.

portals.question: Can the agent plug into our portals and our CRM?
portals.answer: Usually, yes. Most portals send their requests by email, and the agent can read those emails. For the CRM, we use its official connection (API) when it has one, otherwise a file import or a tool like Make. We check your tools during the call, before we put a price on anything, so you know what is possible.

replace.question: Does the assistant replace our negotiators?
replace.answer: No. It answers the questions whose answer is on the property sheet, qualifies the request and offers a slot. As soon as a question needs an opinion, a negotiation or information missing from the sheet, it hands over to a negotiator, with the conversation history. Your team spends less time on the phone and more on viewings.

errors.question: What if the assistant gives wrong information about a property?
errors.answer: It answers only from the data you give it, and says it doesn't know when information is missing. Before launch, we test it on real buyer questions. Every exchange is recorded in a log, so you can fix a property sheet or an instruction as soon as an answer isn't right.

roi.question: How do we know whether AI is worth the cost?
roi.answer: By comparing two numbers: the time the task takes today and the price of the automation. If someone spends five hours a week keying in invoices, the automation is measured against those hours. The AI audit does that calculation task by task. Our prices are set in writing before we start, so the cost doesn't move along the way.

rgpd.question: Can an AI project comply with GDPR?
rgpd.answer: Yes, if it is designed to. Before writing code, we list the personal data the automation handles, keep only what it needs, and set a retention period. Accounts stay in your name. If your data is sensitive, we choose EU hosting or mask some fields before they are sent to the model.

aiAct.question: Does the AI Act apply to our project?
aiAct.answer: Rarely in a heavy way for an SME. Sorting email, extracting invoices or answering product questions are not among the high-risk uses. CV screening or assessing the creditworthiness of individuals are. An assistant that talks to your customers must say it is an AI, and the team using an AI tool must understand its limits. We plan for both. For legal advice, ask your lawyer.

expertise.question: We have no AI skills at all. Is that a problem?
expertise.answer: No, that is the case for most SMEs. We handle the technical side, your team keeps its usual tools and approves what the AI prepares. Every delivery includes onboarding and written documentation, and what we build stays with you: the code in your repository, the n8n or Make automations in your accounts. Nobody needs to know how to write a prompt.

useful.question: How do we know whether AI can help our business?
useful.answer: Think of a task that comes back every week: reading email, re-keying documents, chasing clients. If it follows roughly the same steps each time, it can probably be partly automated. Book a 30-minute call: we pick one with you and tell you honestly whether it's worth it.

continuity.question: What happens if Klyx is no longer available?
continuity.answer: Your project keeps running. The code is in your repository from day one, the n8n or Make automations sit in your accounts with their export, the tools are in your name, and every project ends with a written handover. Any developer can take over from that documentation, without depending on us.
